summary: Every axis the prompt names comes back clean. All five digests re-measure correct, including the two the prompt flags as previously missing — file 07 at d3e95060… and file 10 at 5378cdba… — and the property-pin scoping sentence names the sections actually used. Route C is open with an authority-derivation constraint rather than a closed set, and the closed-set defect is named and rejected in Alternatives by its D-025 provenance. MF-6 is stated non-substitutably in both the decision and the alternatives. D-001 is not amended: the entry restates A/B/C without adding a fourth route, and the decision-type line carries the basis for its RULE-GOVERNED label. D-000 clause 3 is complete. Two SHOULD-FIXes remain, both about accuracy rather than substance. The entry records D-025 as CONTESTED, and no such record exists anywhere in the register — D-025 has no entry at all. And the compression from the superseded entry's eight decision clauses to five drops the one clause that states what consumption does to file 11, in an entry whose title is about consuming file 11.

objections.claim: The header records D-025 as CONTESTED. No CONTESTED record for D-025 exists in the register, and D-025 has no entry of any kind, so the entry attributes a closed-vocabulary status that was never recorded.
objections.evidence: The header reads 'Supersedes: CONTESTED D-017 / D-025 only.' Measured against COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md at 54d34099b33313ef3d9383123a59b962d90fd95bfdfb96c994aac0670da810a4: a grep for entry headings matching '^## D-025' returns nothing — there is no D-025 entry. A sweep for CONTESTED returns ten hits, of which the only cycle record is line 1490, '## D-017 / D-019–D-024 — first completion-sequence cycle (CONTESTED)', whose status line reads 'CONTESTED after three turns under D-000 clause 2. Not adopted.' That record covers D-017 and D-019 through D-024. It does not cover D-025, and no analogous record exists for the D-025–D-031 cycle: of those seven, D-028, D-029 and D-030 are ADOPTED and the remaining four — D-025, D-026, D-027, D-031 — have no entries. So the 'CONTESTED D-017' half is accurate and the 'D-025' half is not. This matters for two reasons beyond tidiness. D-000's status vocabulary is closed and CONTESTED carries a specific meaning — 'no consensus after 3 turns each; parked for the user' — and D-006 turn-2 NOTE-03 records that the closed status vocabulary stays closed. And it misstates the review history: D-025 drew CONSENT from this reviewer at turn 3 of that cycle, so it was not a no-consensus parking; it was simply never adopted.
objections.proposedFix: Restate as 'Supersedes: CONTESTED D-017 and the unadopted D-025 draft only', or record the D-025–D-031 cycle's disposition in the register first and cite it. Either fixes the attribution; the second also closes the gap that four drafts from that cycle currently have no recorded disposition at all.

objections.claim: The compression from the superseded entry's eight decision clauses to five drops the clause stating what consumption does to file 11 — the affirmative half of this entry's own subject — and the no-execution-checklist disclaimer.
objections.evidence: The D-025 turn-3 draft, which I reviewed and consented to, carried eight decision clauses. D-037 carries five, and the mapping is: its 1 = D-025's 1, its 2 = D-025's 2, its 3 = D-025's 3, its 4 = D-025's 4, and its 5 compresses D-025's 5, 6 and the placement half of 7. Two things are not carried. First, D-025 clause 7's leading half: 'After an item becomes live work, file 11 is historical for that item', which D-017 before it stated as 'After consumption, file 11 is historical for that item, not a queue.' D-037's title is 'consume file 11 via D-001 routes' and its clause 3 states how an item becomes live work, but no clause states what becomes of file 11's entry for that item afterwards. That is the affirmative consequence the whole file-11 rule exists to produce, and its absence leaves the anti-queue property resting only on clause 2's rejection of the complete-08-then-turn-to-11 sequence, which addresses ordering rather than per-item status. Second, D-025 clause 8, 'This entry creates no execution checklist.' D-037 has no numbered process of its own and clause 4 defers scheduling to D-036, so the risk is low — I weight this limb lower — but the disclaimer was load-bearing in an entry whose subject is preventing a second checklist, and it was cheap.
objections.proposedFix: Restore both as a sixth clause: 'After an item becomes live work, file 11 is historical for that item, not a queue. This entry creates no execution checklist.'

Closed Route C set: not closed. New forms still need authority from the product-disposition process, D-000, or the user.' MF-6 substitution: refused twice. Clause 3 states 'Per MF-6, any file-08 content change still needs its own D-000-reviewed entry. A product act is not a substitute for that review', and Alternatives carries 'Product packet substitutes for MF-6. Rejected.' Checked against D-001 MF-6's own bytes, which require that register-content changes 'each get their own D-000-reviewed entry and commit' with no alternative offered.

Silent D-001 amendment: none found. Clause 3 restates A/B/C without adding a route and states 'File-08 amendments are not a fourth route'; clause 5 states 'D-001 is not amended.' Neither the five readiness conditions nor SF-3 is quoted or constrained anywhere in the entry.

D-000 clause 3 completeness, field by field against the format at COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md: id, date, title, status, decision, alternatives considered (three, each with a reason), rationale — carried by the decision-type line's basis, 'Restates file 08's only-checklist rule, file 07/10 competing-list disclaimers, file 11's header, and D-001 A/B/C. Adds no fourth route', which is the same form that resolved the identical gap in the D-025 lineage — decision type, reversibility class ('Class: total'), overturn procedure ('C-D037'), readiness effect ('Zero'). Reviewer verdict and commit land at adoption.

The reversibility note's factual claim about D-036 is true, and I checked it against the adopted bytes rather than the draft. D-037 says '(D-036 already states the rule in full)'. Adopted D-036 in the register reads 'Scheduling authorizes drafting only' inside its own decision paragraph, with no citation to D-025 or to any other entry for that rule, and its Depends-on line states 'Does not require D-025.' So the rule is genuinely self-contained in D-036, the conditional hedge 'If D-036's scheduling citation of this rule exists' is safe, and reverting D-037 would strand nothing in D-036.

Clause 4's own citation direction is consistent with adopted bytes: D-037 cites D-036 for scheduling, and adopted D-036 says the same thing in the same terms, so the restatement introduces no conflict.

The RULE-GOVERNED label holds on this text. I checked the specific failure this label has drawn twice in this corpus — an invented closed set presented as a restatement — and it is absent here: the only enumeration is Route C's recording forms, which is explicitly non-exhaustive, and the entry adds no route.
